agent_responses.response_str:
Working correctly — the empty subfields are from the placeholder data. Here's a clear breakdown of the recommended structure:

---

## 📇 vCard: Recommended Field Structure

### Standard fields (universally supported)
```
FN:John Doe              ← Full name
EMAIL:john@example.com   ← Email
TEL:+1-555-123-4567      ← Phone
ADR:;;123 Main St;...    ← Address
```

### `X-` Custom fields (structured, machine-readable)
These use the **vCard extension convention** (`X-` prefix). Each field holds **semicolon-delimited subfields**, just like `ADR` does natively:

```
X-ACCOUNT-ID:ACCT-12345

X-ORDER:ORD-5B048F;2024-11-15;$49.99;Delivered;Widget A,Gadget B
       ↑ order_id  ↑ date      ↑ total ↑ status  ↑ items (comma-sep)

X-PAYMENT:cc_6abb1fab;credit_card;Visa;****4242;12/2026;John Doe
          ↑ id        ↑ type      ↑ brand ↑ masked ↑ exp  ↑ name
```

### `NOTE` field (human-readable fallback)
Apps that ignore `X-` fields will display this. Use `\n` for line breaks:
```
NOTE:Account: ACCT-12345\nOrder: ORD-5B048F / 2024-11-15 / $49.99\n...
```

---

## 📋 JSON: Recommended Structure

JSON is flexible — use **nested objects with descriptive keys**:

```json
{
  "orders": [
    {
      "order_id": "ORD-5B048F",     ← unique identifier
      "date": "2024-11-15",          ← ISO 8601 date
      "total": "$49.99",             ← or numeric: 49.99 + "currency": "USD"
      "status": "Delivered",          ← Delivered | Shipped | Processing | etc.
      "items": ["Widget A"]           ← array of item names
    }
  ],
  "payment_methods": [
    {
      "id": "cc_6abb1fab",            ← payment method token
      "type": "credit_card",          ← credit_card | debit_card | paypal
      "brand": "Visa",                ← card network
      "last_four": "4242",            ← ⚠️ never store full card number
      "exp_month": "12",
      "exp_year": "2026",
      "billing_name": "John Doe"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### ⚠️ Security Tips
- **Never** store full card numbers — only the last 4 digits
- The `id` field (`cc_6abb1fab`) is a **token/reference**, safe to store
- Keep the JSON file in a **secure location** (encrypted folder, password manager)
- The vCard `NOTE`/`X-PAYMENT` fields are **visible to anyone** you share the contact with — omit sensitive details if sharing
